en: Black‑and‑white street scene in a historic European town. Cobblestone road lined with multi‑storey shops and townhouses curves gently toward an ornate building with turrets and a high, steep roof at the end of the street. People in early 20th‑century dress walk along the sidewalks and a horse‑drawn wagon travels up the street. On the right corner is a shop with a large projecting clock and signage for "Paul Richter"; on the left is a shop with an awning carrying the name "Julius Fritsch". The right‑hand shop window advertises various goods such as coffee, sugar, cocoa, tea, cigars, wine, and spirits, described as "Kolonialwaren" (colonial goods) and "Drogen". The overall view resembles a commercial street captured for a postcard.
